name: Kalmak-Ashuu Pass
near: Sary-Bulak — the turn to Kalmak-Ashuu is about 3 km from the village on the Bishkek — Torugart highway (too.kg). The nearest base with services is Kochkor. The earlier “Ken-Suu ~21.6 km” is a straight-line distance from an offset point and is no guide for a traveler.
elev: 3446–3447 m (Trip to Kyrgyzstan, NomadCar, central-asia.live — 3447 m; Nomad's Land, open.kg, OunTravela — 3446 m).
short: Kalmak-Ashuu (3446 m) is a gravel pass over the Song-Kol-Too range, the shortest and most popular road route from Kochkor and Sary-Bulak to the northeast shore of Song-Kol.
desc: The pass links the Bishkek — Naryn highway (the turn near Sary-Bulak) with the Song-Kol basin. The eastern ascent is a steep, stony road through a gorge among scree slopes; the western descent to the lake is gentle, across alpine meadows with edelweiss and herds of yaks. There is constant wind at the top, so there are no yurts on the saddle itself. The road opens in late May (cleared by a snowplow) and closes with the first snow in late October. According to legend, the name is linked to raids by the Kalmyks (Dzungars) on the Kyrgyz at the Song-Kol pastures (Nomad's Land). OunTravela (2026) calls Kalmak-Ashuu the easiest of the passes to Song-Kol — a well-kept gravel road; it is popular with cyclists.
guide: Stop on the Kalmak-Ashuu saddle: from here the Song-Kol basin opens up for the first time — the moment many people take this route for. Up the eastern side the road climbs in steep, stony loops among scree, so don't rush your driver, and at the top keep your jacket handy — the wind here is such that herders don't pitch yurts. Look for edelweiss on the meadows of the western slope and for herds of yaks. A legend says the pass was named by the Kalmyks who once raided the Song-Kol camps. If you're planning a loop route, it's convenient to leave by going down via Moldo-Ashuu to the south or via 33 Parrots to the southeast.
see: The first view of the Song-Kol basin from the 3446 m saddle; the gorge with scree and serpentine on the eastern ascent; alpine meadows with edelweiss on the western slope; herds of yaks; on the way, the Song-Kol-Too and Bay-Dulu ranges (almost 4000 m).
skip: You're going to Song-Kol from the south (from Chayek or Naryn) — Moldo-Ashuu, Kara-Keche or 33 Parrots suit you better. You have an ordinary sedan and no experience with gravel serpentines. You're traveling in November to May: the road is closed by snow.
diff: Moderate for a car: gravel, a steep stony eastern ascent, a gentle western descent; OunTravela (2026) — “the easiest of the passes to Song-Kol”. You need a crossover/4×4 / SUV with good ground clearance (NomadCar). For cyclists, a hard but popular climb.
when: July to September. The road opens in late May after snow clearing and closes in late October (Nomad's Land); Trip to Kyrgyzstan and NomadCar say “June to October”. The herders leave Song-Kol before the pass closes (September).
hours: An open dirt road with no barriers; seasonal — roughly from late May/June to late October, impassable in winter because of snow.
daytime: Morning and the first half of the day: less wind and cloud, soft light on the Song-Kol basin; after rain or at dusk the gravel loops are dangerous (editorial).
how: From Bishkek along the highway toward Naryn via Balykchy and Kochkor to Sary-Bulak; about 3 km from the village is the turn to Kalmak-Ashuu (too.kg), then a gravel climb over the pass and a descent to the northeast shore of Song-Kol. Bishkek — Kochkor about 230 km (~4 h), Kochkor — Song-Kol about 80 km (~2.5 h) according to topologica (2026).
needcar: Yes — a 4×4 / SUV/crossover or an organized transfer; there is no public transport over the pass. An alternative is a bicycle.
self: Yes, in your own/rented car with ground clearance in season; no permit needed. Without a car — only by transfer.
roadtype: Gravel/dirt: the eastern ascent is a steep stony road through a gorge among scree, the western descent is gentle across meadows (Nomad's Land). OunTravela (09.2026) — “a well-kept gravel road”. topologica (2026) warns of deep ruts and the need for high ground clearance.
traveltime: Kochkor — Song-Kol via Kalmak-Ashuu ~80 km / ~2.5 h; Bishkek — Kochkor ~230 km / ~4 h (topologica, 2026). In all, Bishkek — the north shore of Song-Kol ~6.5–7 h with stops (calculated).
stay: There is no accommodation on the pass (because of the wind there are no yurts either — Nomad's Land). Stay overnight in the yurt camps on the north shore of Song-Kol: roughly $15–25/person for budget, $35–50 mid-range, $60–80 full board (topologica, 2026 — estimate, check with CBT Kochkor/Shepherd's Life) — or in Kochkor guesthouses.
net: At Song-Kol the signal is “partial, in places” (too.kg); topologica (2026) reports no mobile signal at most camps. On the pass, operator coverage is not confirmed — rely on offline maps.
entry: Free: no fee for crossing the pass was found. (Separate eco fees at Song-Kol are not confirmed within this entry.)
transfer: Pegas Adventure: Kochkor — Song-Kol via Kalmak-Ashuu — $200 (1 person), $120/person (2), $90/person (3), $80/person (4–12); topologica (2026): $60–80 per car / $15–20 per person with 4 passengers. Marshrutka (minibus) Bishkek — Kochkor — 350 som (CBT Naryn, 05.2026).
bring: A windbreaker and a warm layer (3446 m, strong wind), sunglasses and sunscreen, water and a snack, offline maps; for the driver — a spare tire and a full tank (the last fuel is in Kochkor/Sary-Bulak).
warn: The pass is impassable from late October to late May because of snow. Elevation 3446 m: a same-day climb from Bishkek can cause a headache. In rain the gravel and the loops of the eastern slope are slippery; don't take a sedan. Constant strong wind on the saddle.
food: There is no food on the pass. In the Song-Kol yurt camps — kumys, fresh kaymak, boorsok, beshbarmak (topologica: premium camps include 3 meals, tea and kumys in the price). Before the climb — cafes in Sary-Bulak.
reviews: Google Maps: 5/5, 2 ratings (as of 03.10.2026, from the catalog check). No separate TripAdvisor listing was found. Reviews and blogs (OunTravela, Nomad's Land) mention a spectacular view of Song-Kol and easy gravel; cons — wind, the steep stony ascent, winter closure.
p.sum: Kalmak-Ashuu (3446 m) is the shortest road approach from Kochkor to the northeast shore of Song-Kol: along the highway toward Naryn to Sary-Bulak, a turn after ~3 km, then gravel over the pass — ≈80 km/2.5 h from Kochkor. Open from late May to late October; in dry weather a crossover/SUV can manage it, a sedan is not advised (stony eastern ascent, ruts). Without a car — a 4×4 from Kochkor (≈5200 som per car per 2026 data) or a Pegas Adventure transfer. Fill up in Kochkor; on the pass there are no yurts or services.

p.apps.0.season: Late May (after snow clearing) to late October; best July to September

p.apps.0.haz: Slippery gravel in rain, scree, strong wind, elevation 3446 m; snow at the end of the season

p.onsite.photo_spots: The saddle — a panorama of Song-Kol and the Song-Kol-Too range; the serpentine loops in the gorge on the eastern slope from above.

p.iti.0.title: 2 days Kochkor → Song-Kol → Kochkor
p.iti.0.plan: Day 1: 10:00 Kochkor → 11:00 lunch in Sary-Bulak → 12:30 pass (20 min photos) → 13:30 camp on the north shore, horse ride. Day 2: morning at the lake → back via Kalmak-Ashuu or south via Moldo-Ashuu (check first — in 07.2026 a mudflow destroyed a bridge on the Dyikan — Kara-Keche — Moldo-Ashuu road).
p.iti.1.title: Loop
p.iti.1.plan: Bishkek → Kochkor → Kalmak-Ashuu → Song-Kol → back to Sary-Bulak → Dolon → Naryn → At-Bashy/Tash-Rabat (3–5 days).
p.season: November–May: closed by snow (opened in late May by snow clearing). June: puddles, snow possible. July–August: the best season, camps are full, flowers. September–October: herders leave, few tourists, first snowfalls toward the end of October.
p.budget.economy: ≈6000–9000 som/person for 2 days: marshrutka 350×2, a share of a 4×4 Kochkor—Song-Kol (5200 som/car ×2 /4 ≈2600), yurt with meals 1500–2500, horse 250/hour.
p.budget.comfort: ≈$150–250: Pegas transfer $80–120/person + Ak-Sai camp $85 per yurt + horse $15/hour
p.permits: No permit needed; no fee for crossing the pass was found.
p.access: As a car trip it is accessible to children and older people (views from the car); the 3446 m elevation after a fast ascent can cause a headache. With a stroller — only from the car. With a dog — in the car, yes.
